title: session_ledger row
description: Provisional. One row per play session (a game or launcher log file) or incident (an event record, a dump file, a report folder), joined from session-ledger and history bundles of one machine by scripts/build_session_ledger.py. Provenance points at the byte copy of the source artifact under the ledger output's raw/bundles/<bundle id>/. See docs/session-ledger.md.

entry_id.description: Id: the first 16 hex of SHA-256 over the entry's identity (an event's log, record id, provider, event id and time; a dump file's kind, folder, extension, size and creation time; a report folder's kind, name prefix and creation time; a session's title and creation time, plus its last write time when two logs of that title share a creation time in any input bundle). A rebuild with more bundles keeps the ids of entries already seen, except a session whose creation time first becomes shared when a bundle is added: it is re-keyed with its last write time.

title.description: The game or launcher of a session; for an incident, the title whose allow-listed image name a crash or hang record names, else null.

start_utc.description: Session: the log file's creation time (null when it cannot be trusted, see session_check). Incident: the event's TimeCreated, or a dump or report's creation time.

end_utc.description: Session: the log file's last write time, an inferred end. Incidents are points and have no end.

start_inferred.description: True when the start is a file time taken to stand for the start of play (the log creation time), not a recorded start.

end_inferred.description: True when the end is the log's last write, which can be earlier than the true end (a game that stops writing) and is the end of a session cut short by a freeze.

duration_s.description: end minus start, only when both are known and session_check is ok.

session_check.description: creation_shared: two logs of the title share this creation time in some input bundle (file name tunnelling), so it may be inherited from a log that is gone and the start is unknown; replaced_in_place: a later snapshot shows the file smaller or written earlier, so the start is unknown; end_before_start: the times disagree.

bugcheck_code.description: Kernel-Power 41 only: the named BugcheckCode data item, decimal as Windows records it; null when the record has no named item. Zero is a record with no bug check written.

image_name.description: Only an allow-listed game or launcher image; any other image name is not copied.

file_name.description: A log or dump name the collector kept verbatim; null for a pseudonymised name (pseudonyms are salted per run and do not identify a file across bundles).

component.description: A live kernel dump's component folder.

report_kind.description: The leading word of a Windows Error Reporting report folder name.

observations.description: How many input bundles held this entry; the row is the latest bundle's observation.
